skills.label: Choose a diagram
skills.question: Which visual story best answers the reader's question?
useCases: Route a diagram request by meaning
Choose a renderer after choosing the story
avoidWhen: The user already selected a semantic diagram type
skills.name: diagramming
skills.description: Choose the semantic diagram story first, then select a diagram.zip renderer and produce a clear, reviewable diagram.

skills.label: Diagram workshop
skills.question: What should we discover together before committing to a diagram?
useCases: Facilitate an explicit, user-led diagram design session
avoidWhen: A focused request can be handled directly
skills.name: diagram-workshop
skills.description: Work with me to discover the right diagram question, audience, scope, and level of detail before making a diagram.

skills.label: Review a diagram
skills.role: Does the diagram tell its intended story accurately and accessibly?
question: Review semantics, readability, fidelity, and accessibility
useCases: The request is only to choose a diagram family
skills.name: diagram-review
skills.description: Review a proposed diagram for semantic fit, evidence, readability, accessibility, and renderer or standards limitations; recommend precise revisions.

skills.label: Flowchart
skills.question: What path does work follow through steps and decisions?
avoidWhen: Time-ordered interactions need lifelines
Formal business semantics require BPMN
skills.name: flowchart
skills.description: Choose a flowchart when the user needs a readable decision or process path with a clear start, sequence, branch, merge, or end.

skills.label: Sequence diagram
skills.question: Who communicates with whom, and in what order?
avoidWhen: The main story is static structure
skills.name: sequence-diagram
skills.description: Choose a sequence diagram when the user needs to explain ordered messages, calls, responses, or time-dependent collaboration between participants.

skills.label: State machine diagram
skills.question: Which events cause an entity to change state?
avoidWhen: The story is a sequence of work rather than persistent state
skills.name: state-machine-diagram
skills.description: Choose a state-machine diagram when an entity's permitted states, event-triggered transitions, guards, and entry or exit behavior are the central story.

skills.label: Activity diagram
skills.question: How does work flow across actions, branches, and owners?
avoidWhen: The process requires executable BPMN semantics
skills.name: activity-diagram
skills.description: Choose an activity diagram when the user needs to explain workflow logic, parallel work, decisions, joins, and responsibility across actions.

skills.label: BPMN process
skills.question: How does a formal business process coordinate work, events, and participants?
avoidWhen: A lightweight explanatory flow is sufficient
skills.name: bpmn-process
skills.description: Choose BPMN when the user needs a formal business-process model with events, tasks, gateways, pools, lanes, and message or sequence flows.

skills.label: Use-case diagram
skills.question: Which actors pursue which goals through the system?
avoidWhen: Detailed interaction order or internal design is required
skills.name: use-case-diagram
skills.description: Use when the user needs to explain who can achieve which externally visible goals with a system, including actors, system boundaries, and goal relationships.

skills.label: Data-flow diagram
skills.question: Where does data originate, move, transform, and rest?
avoidWhen: Control flow or message timing is the main concern
skills.name: data-flow-diagram
skills.description: Use when the user needs to show where information originates, how processes transform it, where stores retain it, and which external entities exchange it.

skills.label: Timeline
skills.question: What happened, or will happen, in chronological order?
avoidWhen: Durations and dependencies drive the story
skills.name: timeline
skills.description: Use when the user needs to communicate events or milestones in chronological order, with dates, intervals, eras, or parallel tracks.

skills.label: Gantt chart
skills.question: When do tasks occur, overlap, and depend on each other?
avoidWhen: Only milestone chronology is needed
skills.name: gantt-chart
skills.description: Use when the user needs a time-scaled schedule showing tasks, durations, dependencies, milestones, and progress across teams or workstreams.

skills.label: User journey map
skills.question: What does a person experience across stages of a goal?
avoidWhen: The request is for system behavior without a user-experience lens
skills.name: user-journey-map
skills.description: Use when the user needs to understand a person’s experience across stages, touchpoints, actions, thoughts, emotions, pain points, and opportunities.

skills.label: Choose an architecture diagram
skills.question: Which abstraction level and viewpoint will answer the architecture question?
useCases: Route among landscape, context, container, component, dynamic, and deployment views
avoidWhen: The user already selected an architecture view
skills.name: choose-architecture-diagram
skills.description: Choose the smallest architecture view that answers the stakeholder's question, then route it to a suitable diagram source.

skills.label: System landscape diagram
skills.question: How do systems and people relate across an organization or domain?
avoidWhen: The focus is one system and its immediate environment
skills.name: system-landscape-diagram
skills.description: Show the systems and people across an organization or domain, emphasizing ownership and meaningful dependencies.

skills.label: System context diagram
skills.question: How does one system interact with people and external systems?
avoidWhen: Internal applications or deployable units must be shown
skills.name: system-context-diagram
skills.description: Explain one system in its environment by showing its users, external systems, and the relationships that matter.

skills.label: Container diagram
skills.question: What deployable or runnable units make up the system?
avoidWhen: Code-level components or infrastructure instances are the focus
skills.name: container-diagram
skills.description: Show the major deployable or runtime containers inside one software system and how they collaborate.

skills.label: Component diagram
skills.question: Which components collaborate inside a container or subsystem?
avoidWhen: Only system-level scope is needed
skills.name: component-diagram
skills.description: Create a component-level view of software structure, interfaces, and dependencies when the audience needs implementation boundaries rather than deployment topology.

skills.label: Architecture dynamic diagram
skills.question: How do architecture elements collaborate for one scenario?
avoidWhen: A reusable protocol sequence needs detailed lifelines
skills.name: architecture-dynamic-diagram
skills.description: Explain an architecture scenario over time by showing participating components, messages, and state changes for one concrete use case.

skills.label: Deployment diagram
skills.question: Where do software instances run, and how are they connected?
avoidWhen: Logical structure without runtime placement is enough
skills.name: deployment-diagram
skills.description: Show where software artifacts run, which infrastructure nodes host them, and how runtime communication crosses environments or trust boundaries.

skills.label: Block diagram
skills.question: What are the major functional blocks and their interfaces?
avoidWhen: A stricter domain notation is required
skills.name: block-diagram
skills.description: Arrange labeled blocks and relationships to communicate system decomposition, signal or data paths, and high-level structure without committing to a specialized formal notation.

skills.label: Class diagram
skills.question: What types exist and how are their structures related?
avoidWhen: The main story concerns data persistence tables
skills.name: class-diagram
skills.description: Create or review class diagrams that explain types, responsibilities, contracts, and structural relationships in an object-oriented or domain model.

skills.label: Entity-relationship diagram
skills.question: Which data entities exist and how are they related?
avoidWhen: Runtime object behavior is the focus
skills.name: entity-relationship-diagram
skills.description: Model persistent data with entities, attributes, keys, relationships, cardinality, optionality, and integrity boundaries using an entity-relationship diagram.

skills.label: Dependency graph
skills.question: What depends on what, and where are cycles or critical paths?
avoidWhen: Ordered interactions or physical topology are central
skills.name: dependency-graph
skills.description: Show dependencies between packages, modules, services, artifacts, or concepts when the important story is coupling, direction, reachability, or change impact.

skills.label: Network topology
skills.question: Which network zones, devices, and links connect?
avoidWhen: Application behavior rather than connectivity is the focus
skills.name: network-topology
skills.description: Document physical or logical networks with nodes, interfaces, links, segments, addressing, trust zones, and traffic boundaries.

skills.label: Mind map
skills.question: What ideas radiate from one central topic?
avoidWhen: Relationships need explicit semantic labels
skills.name: mind-map
skills.description: Use when the user needs to explore one central topic through associative branches, capture brainstorming, or organize an unconstrained idea space before choosing a structure.

skills.label: Concept map
skills.question: Which concepts relate, and what do those relationships mean?
avoidWhen: A single-root hierarchy is sufficient
skills.name: concept-map
skills.description: Use when the user needs to explain concepts and the labeled relationships between them, especially definitions, dependencies, evidence, or cross-domain connections.

skills.label: Hierarchy diagram
skills.question: How is a set organized into parent-child levels?
avoidWhen: Many-to-many relationships carry the meaning
skills.name: hierarchy-diagram
skills.description: Use when the user needs a ranked, nested, or reporting structure such as a taxonomy, organization chart, tree, or work breakdown structure.

skills.label: Decision tree
skills.question: Which choices or tests lead to which outcomes?
avoidWhen: The goal is to depict an operational process with loops
skills.name: decision-tree
skills.description: Use when the user needs to show a sequence of choices, branching rules, outcomes, or diagnostic paths.

skills.label: Matrix diagram
skills.question: How do items compare across two dimensions?
avoidWhen: Geometric set overlap or time is the main encoding
skills.name: matrix-diagram
skills.description: Use when the user needs to compare two dimensions, expose a portfolio or prioritization space, or show a many-to-many relationship in a grid or quadrant.

skills.label: Set diagram
skills.question: How do categories overlap or contain one another?
avoidWhen: Exact quantities or many sets must be compared
skills.name: set-diagram
skills.description: Use when the user needs to show membership, overlap, exclusion, union, intersection, or nested categories with sets.

skills.label: Choose a data visualization
skills.question: Which visual encoding best supports the analytical task and data?
avoidWhen: The request is a conceptual diagram rather than a quantitative display
skills.name: choose-data-visualization
skills.description: Choose and design a data visualization when the user has data, a comparison, trend, distribution, relationship, flow, or geographic question but has not yet chosen a chart form. Use the simplest honest encoding, explain the story, and route the result to Vega or Vega-Lite when appropriate.

skills.label: Protocol layout diagram
skills.question: How are bits or bytes allocated within a protocol record?
avoidWhen: Message ordering or state transitions are the focus
skills.name: protocol-layout-diagram
skills.description: Use when a diagram must explain the bit, byte, or word layout of a protocol message, file header, register, or binary record.

skills.label: Digital timing diagram
skills.question: How do digital signals change relative to time and each other?
avoidWhen: The request is for an analog waveform plot
skills.name: digital-timing-diagram
skills.description: Use when a diagram must show digital signals changing over time, including clocked interfaces, bus transactions, handshakes, setup/hold relationships, or waveform protocols.

skills.label: Rack diagram
skills.question: Which equipment occupies each rack unit?
avoidWhen: Logical network connectivity is the primary story
skills.name: rack-diagram
skills.description: Use when documenting equipment placement in a cabinet or rack, including rack units, device identity, power, network uplinks, and physical capacity.

skills.label: Wiring harness diagram
skills.question: How do connectors, conductors, and terminations map?
avoidWhen: Circuit behavior or board-level electronics are the focus
skills.name: wiring-harness-diagram
skills.description: Use when the user needs to document wires, cables, connectors, splices, branches, pin mappings, or harness manufacturing/service information.

skills.label: HDL component diagram
skills.question: How do HDL modules, ports, and signal paths connect?
avoidWhen: Gate-level timing or physical wiring is the focus
skills.name: hdl-component-diagram
skills.description: Use when the user needs a hardware-design view of HDL entities, modules, interfaces, ports, parameters, clocks, resets, and hierarchy.

skills.label: Circuit diagram
skills.question: Which electronic components connect into a circuit?
avoidWhen: Physical harness routing or enclosure placement is needed
skills.name: circuit-diagram
skills.description: Use when the user needs an electrical or electronic schematic showing components, nets, reference designators, power, signal flow, and test points.

skills.label: Technical illustration
skills.question: Which spatial or mechanical relationships must the reader see?
avoidWhen: Abstract relationships can be communicated more precisely with a diagram notation
skills.name: technical-illustration
skills.description: Use when the user needs an explanatory technical figure showing parts, assemblies, operation, dimensions, callouts, or a controlled visual sequence.

standards.name: OMG BPMN 2.0.2
standards.note: The BPMN renderer accepts BPMN 2.0 XML and diagram interchange data. Treat rendering as separate from complete semantic validation.

standards.name: OMG UML 2.5.1
standards.note: PlantUML and other renderers cover useful UML views, but diagram.zip does not validate the complete metamodel or import and export UML XMI and UMLDI.

integration.scope: UML XMI/UMLDI import, model validation, profile handling, and round-trip fidelity

standards.name: ISO 5807:1985
standards.note: General renderers can apply its flowchart conventions, but diagram.zip does not validate symbol or path conformance.

standards.name: RFC 2360 packet diagram conventions
standards.note: PacketDiag and Bytefield can express layouts that follow the conventions, but protocol-specific validation is not built in.

standards.name: OMG DMN 1.5
standards.note: Informal decision trees are supported. Decision requirements diagrams, DMN XML interchange, and FEEL evaluation are not.

integration.scope: DMN XML parser, decision requirements rendering, validation, and optional FEEL evaluation

standards.name: The Open Group ArchiMate 3.2
standards.note: Generic architecture pictures are supported, but ArchiMate viewpoints, notation rules, and model exchange are not.

integration.scope: Licensed notation assets, ArchiMate 3.x model exchange, viewpoint rules, and conformance testing

standards.name: OMG SysML 2.0
standards.note: Generic blocks and relationships are supported, but SysML language semantics, textual notation, model interchange, and view validation are not.

integration.scope: SysML textual or JSON parsing, KerML/SysML semantics, libraries, view generation, and conformance

standards.name: IEC 60617:2026 DB
standards.note: General renderers can draw circuits and harnesses, but diagram.zip has no licensed IEC symbol library or symbol validation.

integration.scope: Symbol licensing, searchable assets, semantic ports and nets, document rules, and conformance boundaries
